title: Comment on "Distinct Behaviors of Inner and Outer CuO$_2$ Planes in Quadruple-Layer Cuprate (Cu,C)Ba$_2$Ca$_3$Cu$_4$O$_{11 + δ}$"
abstract: In a recent Letter, Sun et al. report photoemission spectroscopy measurements on the four-layer cuprate (Cu,C)Ba2Ca3Cu4O11 (CuC-1234) in which they resolve two superconducting gaps associated with the inner (IP) and outer (OP) CuO2 planes. CuC-1234 has a Tc as 117 K in a sample previously structurally characterized using neutron powder diffraction. From the Luttinger sum, the beta-band of the IP was found to be heavily underdoped (p~0.07) while the OP alpha2 bonding band was strongly overdoped (p~0.25). Each revealed a gap with very different momentum and temperature dependences. A large gap on the beta band was found to close at the bulk Tc, while a smaller gap on the alpha2 band closed at 70 K. Such two-gap behavior would indicate weak-coupling between the IP and OP, resulting in a second gap-opening temperature, Tc2, and implying a two-step development of the superfluid density on cooling, first on the IPs then on the OPs. Here, we point out that the observed values of Tc and Tc2 are fully consistent with a long-standing correlation of Tc with a bond-valence sum parameter, V+, calculated from the crystallographic bond lengths. This suggests that Tc2 in the OP is entirely consistent with the local structure of the OP where the value of V+(OP) is reduced by the presence of the apical oxygens and Tc2 reduced accordingly. It is as though two largely decoupled superconductors are present in the single 1234 compound and their individual pairing temperatures are determined by their local nearest-neighbour structure, reflecting the very short-range physics.
summary: This work analyzes the two-gap superconductivity in a quadruple-layer cuprate, suggesting that the inner and outer $	ext{CuO}_2$ planes act as largely decoupled superconductors. The key finding is that the critical temperatures for both gaps correlate strongly with the local structural parameter, the Bond-Valence Sum ($V^+$), implying that pairing is governed by short-range, local electronic structure rather than bulk properties.
main_problem: The paper investigates the distinct superconducting pairing mechanisms and critical temperatures in the quadruple-layer cuprate $	ext{(Cu,C)}	ext{Ba}_2	ext{Ca}_3	ext{Cu}_4	ext{O}_{11+\delta}$ by analyzing the separate superconducting gaps in the inner and outer $	ext{CuO}_2$ planes.
main_result: The observed two-gap superconductivity suggests two largely decoupled superconducting planes, each governed by its local crystal structure, as evidenced by the consistency of $T_{c2}$ with the Bond-Valence Sum parameter ($V^+$) calculated locally.
method: The analysis combines photoemission spectroscopy results (revealing two gaps) with structural calculations using the Bond-Valence Sum ($V^+$) parameter derived from crystallographic bond lengths.
model_or_system: The physical system is the quadruple-layer cuprate $	ext{(Cu,C)}	ext{Ba}_2	ext{Ca}_3	ext{Cu}_4	ext{O}_{11+\delta}$, which exhibits superconductivity in two distinct $	ext{CuO}_2$ planes (Inner and Outer). The underlying physics is modeled by analyzing the superconducting gaps and their dependence on local structural parameters.
key_observables: Two superconducting gaps ($	ext{IP}$ and $	ext{OP}$), bulk critical temperature ($T_c$), second gap-opening temperature ($T_{c2}$), and the Bond-Valence Sum parameter ($V^+$).
important_parameters: Doping levels ($p$): $	ext{IP}$ ($ eta$-band) is heavily underdoped ($p \approx 0.07$); $	ext{OP}$ ($\alpha_2$ band) is strongly overdoped ($p \approx 0.25$).
main_assumptions: The primary assumption is that the superconducting pairing temperatures are determined by the local nearest-neighbor structure, quantified by the $V^+$ parameter, suggesting weak coupling between the planes.
figures_summary: Figure 1 plots the maximum critical temperature ($T_{c,	ext{max}}$) against the Bond-Valence Sum parameter ($V^+$) for various cuprates, including specific data points for $T_c$ and $T_{c2}$ versus $V^+(	ext{IP})$ and $V^+(	ext{OP})$ for $	ext{CuC-1234}$.
paper_structure: The paper first presents the observation of two distinct superconducting gaps in $	ext{CuC-1234}$. It then correlates the measured $T_c$ and $T_{c2}$ values with the structural Bond-Valence Sum parameter ($V^+$). Finally, it discusses the implications of this correlation, suggesting local structural control over pairing temperatures.
why_interesting: The concept of two distinct, locally governed superconducting gaps in a single material provides a concrete example of emergent, multi-component superconductivity, which has parallels in understanding complex, multi-band correlated superconductors.
